ai.description: This sea krait reaches 1.5 meters. It features a blue-grey body with black bands, a distinct yellow snout, and a paddle-like tail. It possesses a subcylindrical body and ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Yellow-lipped Sea Krait is best identified by its distinct yellow snout and upper lip, which contrast sharply with its black-and-white banded body.
ai.habitat: The yellow-lipped sea krait inhabits tropical coastal waters, frequently emerging onto rocky shores and mangrove forests to rest, digest, and lay eggs.
ai.behavior: The yellow-lipped sea krait is amphibious, spending significant time on land to digest prey, shed its skin, and lay eggs before returning to the ocean to hunt.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laticauda colubrina* is oviparous, laying clutches of 1–10 eggs on land. In India, nesting typically occurs between September and December.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laticauda colubrina* is found along the eastern and western coasts of the Indian subcontinent, specifically inhabiting coastal waters and islands like the Andamans.
